threads.body: [General] The negotiated protocol version is snapshotted when `sendRequest` creates the cold tool-call `Mono`, but initialize only stores that version when its publisher emits. A common composition such as `client.initialize().then(client.callTool(...))` constructs the tool publisher before initialization completes, so the later tool span and metric permanently omit `mcp.protocol.version`. Resolve the session's protocol version inside the deferred subscription path (before `instrumenter().start`) instead of during `prepare`, and cover this composed initialization/tool-call flow.

replies.body: Good catch. I moved the protocol-version lookup into the deferred subscription path immediately before `instrumenter().shouldStart/start`, while preserving a per-subscription request snapshot. I also added regression coverage for `initialize().then(callTool(...))` at both the public async-client E2E level and the session span/metric level. Fixed in 2adb03c4.

threads.body: [Javaagent] This `_meta` copy is shared by every subscription of the returned Mono, but propagation is injected on each subscription. If one subscription has W3C baggage and a later subscription has none, the baggage propagator writes nothing on the later injection. The earlier baggage remains in the outgoing request, leaking context between operations. Preserve an untouched application-metadata snapshot and give each subscription its own request and propagation carrier. Add a regression test that resubscribes with different baggage contexts.

[Javaagent] If a configured propagator throws here, the span has already started but its completion handlers have not been installed. The outer catch returns the original publisher, so the span never ends and its duration metric is lost even if the tool call succeeds. Catch injection failures locally and continue installing the completion handlers. Add coverage with a throwing propagator to verify that the application result and telemetry completion are preserved.

threads.body: [Javaagent] In SDK 0.14.1, `HttpClientStreamableHttpTransport.sendMessage()` invokes the application request customizer inside this propagated MCP CLIENT context. Independent outgoing work started by the customizer therefore inherits the tool-call span instead of the caller context. Capture the caller context separately and restore it around customizer invocation and its returned publisher, retaining the outgoing context for SDK execution and propagation; cover this with the real HTTP transport.

[Javaagent] With `Context.root()` as the caller context, synchronous downstream callbacks can run under this MCP CLIENT scope because Reactor's `TracingSubscriber` skips restoring root. Another tool call started in `doOnNext` or `onErrorResume` can therefore inherit the ended CLIENT span or be suppressed. Explicitly restore the captured caller context at downstream signal boundaries, including root, while preserving the outgoing context for SDK execution; cover a callback that starts another tool call without an ambient parent.
